title: Destructive paths ignoring a documented classification or sentinel
description: Two data-loss bugs had the same shape: the meaning was written down, but the code that deletes data never checked it. (1) phase25 typed the WAL scan's tail (`TailKind`: Incomplete, ChecksumMismatch, Blank, Unreadable) and documented that a crash never leaves an Unreadable record, yet `wal_frame::repair`, the only code that truncates the WAL, still truncated every `ScanEnd::TornTail` with `..` in its pattern, so startup silently deleted acknowledged records a newer release wrote. (2) `StreamConfig::retention_secs` documented `0 = infinite`, but `Room::compact` computed `now - 0` and dropped every event. Rules: (1) when you add a classification, grep every consumer that destroys data and make it match on the new field (no `..` over it); (2) a sentinel value documented on a config field must be special-cased at each read site, with a test that uses the sentinel against old data; (3) when a removal path updates derived state (here a room's `min_offset` and stats), test the case where it removes everything, and remove only a prefix of an offset-indexed buffer so contiguity holds even when timestamps step back. (4) a guard that looks only at the first bad item is not enough when the decision also depends on what follows it: the WAL scan decides "torn tail" by searching for a frame after the first invalid one, and that search counted only decodable frames, so a damaged frame followed by an undecodable record was still truncated with it; the search must use the same notion of "intact" (checksum matches, long enough) as the classification, and the tests must cover both orders. Fixed in phase34 (`PersistenceError::WALUnreadableRecord`, `wal_frame::find_intact_frame`, `Room::compact`).
